sources.title: How My Predictions Are Faring — Ray Kurzweil
sources.locator: P01 printed p.29, Computers #21; P02 opening 2009 paragraph

sourceCaveat: The original book edition has not been independently checked. See the listed source and full record for attribution limits.

reference.criterion: A roughly $1,000 PC can supply about 10^12 peak single-precision operations per second, counting its graphics processor.
reference.rationale: AMD’s 2008 $199–$299 GPU generation supplied about 1–1.2 TFLOPS; the remaining budget could accommodate an ordinary host PC. This is a reasonable numerical hardware hit. It is not a claim that every program sustains a teraflop or that GPU and CPU work are interchangeable.

strict.criterion: The entire PC sustains a teraflop on a specified general-purpose benchmark, rather than adding peak GPU arithmetic.
strict.rationale: Peak board specifications do not establish the stricter 2009 system benchmark. Later consumer hardware has ample headroom, so the narrower practical-throughput reading is late.
